page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 32-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features a dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per physical core, providing 32 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, equating to 4.0 GB per core, and a 128 MB L3 cache. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

In benchmark testing, the D32pds_v6 demonstrates top-tier memory performance, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 448.6 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 188.32 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tiers, while single-core performance and LLM inference tasks generally fall into the average range. Large-model prompt processing represents a performance tradeoff, scoring in the lower percentile.

The ARM-based architecture of the Dpdsv6 family delivers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads. By utilizing dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, it avoids resource contention. This profile makes the D32pds_v6 highly suitable for database hosting, Redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation tasks.
